Hi [CLIENT_NAME_001]! I really appreciate your kind comments and your honesty about the budget. Knowing that upfront makes it much easier to determine the best fit.

Instead of charging by the hour, I use flat project pricing, which most clients find simpler. Before we begin, you’ll know exactly what is included and what the total cost will be, so there aren’t any surprises.

My standard resume and cover letter package begins at $150. It includes an in-depth intake so I can understand your experience and objectives, a completely ATS-optimized resume provided in Word and PDF, a customized cover letter, and one revision round to ensure everything feels right to you.

Once I’ve received everything I need from you, the usual turnaround time is 2-3 business days.

If the budget is limiting you at the moment, I’m glad to discuss alternatives. In some cases, it works better to begin with only the resume and add the cover letter when you’re ready. Whichever route you choose, I want you to receive something that will genuinely work for you.

What kind of timeline are you working with, and do you know which types of roles you plan to pursue?
Besides the "standard" option, what other packages are available?
What i'm really trying to understand is what you mean by "standard"

In terms of deliverables, standard includes a completely ATS-optimized resume in Word and PDF, a customized cover letter, and one revision round.
Given the current hiring market, I’ve started producing both a "Standard" version and a "Signature" version of the resume for many clients.

**Standard Edition**
This is the streamlined, professional option focused on functionality. It is fully ATS-optimized, so the formatting is designed to make it through the automated screening systems that most employers use before a person reviews the resume. You’ll receive editable Word and PDF copies. It’s the best fit when you’re submitting online applications and need a polished document that is ready for recruiters.

**Signature Edition**
This includes everything offered with the Standard, along with a visually designed version created in Canva and branded specifically for you. It has a modern, attention-grabbing look and works well when sent straight to a hiring manager, shared during networking events, or added to your portfolio. It can stand out in ways that a conventional resume cannot. Most clients select this tier when visual presentation is just as important as the written content.

**Cover Letter**
This is a completely customized letter that matches your voice and is targeted toward the role you want. Rather than using a generic template, I create a genuine narrative that supports your resume and gives you a compelling message. As with the resumes, I produce both a standard cover letter and a signature version that follows the design developed for your signature edition resume.

Many clients choose to include LinkedIn Optimization in their package as well. This involves much more than transferring resume content to the profile. I rewrite the headline, About section, and experience entries so they work with LinkedIn’s search algorithm and improve the chances of recruiters finding you. I also provide guidance about keywords, profile settings, and positioning yourself for your target roles.

Where are you in the process—are you currently submitting applications, or are you still beginning to work out your next step? Do you have a budget range in mind?
I genuinely try to work with people based on where they’re at!

They definitely aren’t lol. Unfortunately, resumes are now being processed through ATS (Applicant Tracking System) software that collects the information. That’s why we use the Standard—it can make it through that system and reach the appropriate people. The Signature edition, meanwhile, is something you can send straight to hiring managers, take to interviews, use while networking, etc.
Oh no! I believe you can fix it by opening Settings and going to Contact Info!
Is there a difference between the standard and the signature?
I’m asking since I don't have a linkedin.
This may sound ridiculous, but i'm strongly opposed to social media platforms and try to remain off the grid
Were you asking whether the two are different?
Being on social media negatively affects my mental health
Although, I suppose it isn't truly a social media platform; it's really more about networking
At my previous job, for example, they brought in a professional photographer to photograph everyone for the website, and I wouldn’t participate

In brief, both contain identical content. Each version follows the exact same writing process, including the same research, strategy, and carefully developed bullet points. Presentation is the only distinction.

The Standard is a professionally formatted, clean Word/PDF file. It prioritizes performance: it is ATS-friendly, straightforward to read, and fully suitable for every type of application.

The Signature uses all of that same content but presents it through a designed format, with a custom layout, typography, and visual branding created in Canva. It’s intended to catch someone’s attention when it appears in their inbox. Many clients use the two versions differently: the Standard for online submissions involving ATS, and the Signature for networking or direct outreach where visual differentiation is important.

And yeah, neither version has anything to do with the LinkedIn add on—that’s an entirely separate process lol. I also completely understand your feelings about social media. That’s a different subject altogether, and it can absolutely be harmful.
What is the price for the Signature Edition?
The resume and cover letter package would cost $200

Share any specific roles or job postings you're considering. At the very least, send the job titles and industries you intend to target. Greater specificity is always more helpful.

**Background info:** provide a brief overview of your employment history, major achievements, skills, and anything else you believe distinguishes you. Rough notes or bullet points are perfectly acceptable for now.

You can send the information in any format. Whether it’s a disorganized Word doc, several paragraphs, or an informal job list, I can work with it. Having more information allows me to tell your story more effectively.

Please give a little extra attention to these sections:

Hi [CLIENT_NAME_001],

Your first drafts are ready to review! I’ve attached the Standard and Signature editions of both your resume and cover letter, for four documents total.

Here’s a quick explanation of what you’re reviewing:

The **Standard editions** are the ATS-optimized Word and PDF versions. They’re designed to make it through automated screening systems when you apply online, while remaining clean, professional, and easy for you to update later.

The **Signature editions** are the designed Canva versions. They’re branded specifically to you and intended to stand out when you send them directly to a hiring manager, use them while networking, or follow up after a conversation. The content is the same, but the presentation is different.

A few notes as you go through everything:

Because there were some blank areas in your questionnaire, I used your old resume to make a few educated guesses and fill the gaps. The main ones involve your timeline—San Jose Options as 2010 to 2021, your independent personal assistant work as 2011 to 2021, and Teamraderie from April 2021 forward—as well as the positioning. I targeted Executive/Personal Assistant roles because that is where your experience is strongest. I also removed Macy's because it is older than 20 years and did not contribute to the overall story.

I’ve also attached a brief follow-up document containing a handful of quick questions. Most are meant to verify dates and identify a few specific accomplishments from your Teamraderie role. Even a few words in response to each question will help me sharpen the next draft considerably.

Please take your time reviewing it all. Once you’re ready, send me any edits, reactions, or answers to the questions, and I’ll incorporate them. Your first round of revisions is included, so please be candid now about what feels right and what does not.

I’m looking forward to hearing your thoughts!

Hi [CLIENT_NAME_001],

I’m so sorry. I had reviewed your answers, but at some point I mistakenly got it into my head that I was waiting for a response from you—my fault! Your answers were extremely helpful, and I’ve now updated both the resume and cover letter to incorporate everything you shared. The new versions are attached.

Here are a few notes about the updates:

The largest change is the overall positioning. Since you said you’re open to trying something new and are not necessarily focused on assistant roles, I reworked the resume around remote operations. The headline, summary, and core competencies now emphasize operations, logistics, customer relations, and process building. This positions you for a much broader range of remote opportunities—operations coordinator, customer operations, logistics coordinator, project coordinator, and similar roles—while retaining your personal assistant experience in your work history. The cover letter takes the same approach and clearly identifies the types of roles you’re open to, so hiring managers do not have to guess.

I corrected the timeline as well. San Jose Options is now listed as 2010 to 2014, while your independent personal assistant work is shown as 2011 to Present with a small "(Concurrent)" note. That note makes it clear that the overlap with Teamraderie is intentional rather than confusing, but it is completely optional, so let me know if you prefer to remove it.

Your FIDM credential is also listed correctly now as Associate of Arts in Merchandise Marketing. For Teamraderie, I placed more emphasis on your answer that you "built everything from the ground up." That became one of the resume’s strongest sections and makes your builder mindset very clear.

If anything seems wrong—dates that should be changed, wording that does not sound like you, missing information, or anything else—let me know and I’ll incorporate it.

Please take your time; there’s no rush.

Thank you,
